Question: The solutions to the equations \(z^2 = 4 + 4\sqrt{15}\,i\) and \(z^2 = 2 + 2\sqrt{3}\,i,\) where \(i = \sqrt{-1},\) form the vertices of a parallelogram in the complex plane. The area of this parallelogram can be written in the form \(p\sqrt{q} - r\sqrt{s},\) where \(p,\) \(q,\) \(r,\) and \(s\) are positive integers and neither \(q\) nor \(s\) is divisible by the square of any prime number. What is \(p + q + r + s?\)
